Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems.
